chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding a slave who is owned by partners, if one of them sells his share, his companion says, 'I am more rightful to it.' Would that be for him? He said: 'Yes, if there is one (partner).'
It was said, 'Is there shuf'ah (preemption) regarding animals?' So he said: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of preemption (shuf'ah) for co-owned slaves and animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the application of shuf'ah (preemption) in co-owned property, specifically distinguishing between human slaves and animals. It establishes that while a co-owner has priority to buy out a selling partner's share in a slave, this right is explicitly denied for animals, reflecting the juristic consensus on the nature of ownership rights in these categories. This distinction highlights the nuanced approach of Shia fiqh in applying preemption rules based on the specific characteristics of the commodity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘With regards to the owned slave who happens to be between the partners, so one of them sells him, and his companion says, ‘I am more rightful with it’. Would that be for him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when there was one (partner)’.
So it was said, is there any right of ‘شُفْعَةٌ’ (preference to the sale to the near ones) regarding animals?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

This is about the case of a slave who is owned by several people and one of them sells his share and the other says, ‘I am more rightful to buy it if his claim is right.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a right if there is only one shareholder.’
It then was asked if there is right of al-Shuf’ (priority right over others to buy) in the sale of animals. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, there is no right of al-Shuf ’ in the sale of animals.’”
